title: Human Rights Judge Navi Pillay Wins the Nobel Peace Prize
summary:
Navi Pillay, a judge and human rights lawyer from South Africa, has won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize. The prize was announced on Friday.

The Nobel Committee called Pillay a "legal pioneer" with exceptional courage and integrity. It said it chose her at a time when "institutions of international law are under political attack." International law is the set of rules countries agree to follow, including rules meant to protect people during wars.

Pillay grew up in South Africa under apartheid, a system that treated people unfairly based on their race. She is of Indian descent and faced deep discrimination. Allan Ngari of the group Human Rights Watch said her rise to the top of the legal world should inspire people from disadvantaged communities everywhere.

Pillay has had a long career in world courts. She is now a judge on the International Court of Justice, a United Nations court. She once led the UN's human rights office. She was also a judge at the International Criminal Court and at a special court set up to deal with crimes committed during the 1994 genocide in Rwanda.

Stephen Rapp, a former US ambassador for war crimes issues, worked in courtrooms where Pillay was a judge. He said her rulings in Rwanda helped the world treat harm done to women and girls during war as a serious crime for the first time. He said her work has always been based on facts and the law, with deep respect for victims and survivors.

Pillay heard the news while at a center in Nuremberg, Germany, where the first trials of Nazi leaders took place 80 years ago. Hours after the announcement, the US government announced sanctions on the International Criminal Court.
why_it_matters: The prize highlights the role of international courts at a time when the Nobel Committee says they are under political attack, and the same day the US sanctioned one of those courts.

background_read: The Nobel Peace Prize is a famous international award given each year to a person or group who has worked to promote peace.

International courts, such as the International Court of Justice and the International Criminal Court, are places where disputes between countries are settled or people are tried for the most serious crimes.
South Africa's apartheid system kept people apart by race and denied many people equal rights until it ended in the 1990s.
After the genocide in Rwanda, a special international court was set up to hold those responsible accountable.
